subject: Clarify: region pinning commitments & subprocessor swap / transient cross-zone processing
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@medicore.com>, MediCore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Residency guarantees and operator/subprocessor swap policy

Hi Diego —

Thanks for the product overview during last week's call. Before we move forward with procurement, Legal and ProdOps asked me to confirm a couple of technical/contractual points about Redwood's residency commitments and how you manage subprocessor/operator changes that might touch customer data across regions. Short list below:  

1) Can Redwood provide a formal commitment to pin customer workloads to APAC (Singapore) and EU (Frankfurt) for both compute and egress, with the only exception being a defined transient failover window for emergency redundancy? If so, what is the maximum transient window (hours) and how is it limited in the DPA?

2) If a Redwood subprocessor (or operator node) needs to be swapped or rebalanced and that results in ephemeral cross-zone processing, what notice do you provide to customers and what is the policy for sensitive data (PII, PHI)? We'd prefer at minimum 48h notice and a rolling strategy that avoids bulk reingestion in another jurisdiction.

3) For any transient cross-region processing, what telemetry is retained and for how long? We need assurance the platform doesn't replicate logs that include raw payloads outside the pinned region.

4) Can you share the current subprocessor roster and a redlined DPA annex that covers subprocessor swap notification and KMS handling during failover?

If helpful I can put our Legal and Security folks on a quick call. We're close to signing but these items are gating approval for our compliance team.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Ortiz
Head of ProdOps, MediCore
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency guarantees and operator/subprocessor swap policy

Hi Lena —

Appreciate the clear list. TL;DR: we can commit to region-affinity pinning with narrow, auditable transient windows for failover; we propose a 72-hour notification baseline for planned operator/subprocessor swaps and 1) limited telemetry retention rules and 2) a DPA annex we can redline. Details below.

1) Region pinning: For customers that require it we offer a Region Affinity SLA. That pins compute and egress to the requested region (ap-sg or eu-de) except under these limited circumstances: 
  - Planned maintenance (scheduled within the SLA)
  - Unplanned failover (regional outage)
  - Emergency operator swaps to remediate an active incident

For planned maintenance we provide advance notice and an ops-runbook. For regional outages we allow transient cross-zone processing to maintain availability; our standard transient window is documented as up to 72 hours in the DPA annex. We can discuss tightening to 48 hours for MediCore as a commercial exception.

2) Subprocessor/operator swap notice: We publish a subprocessor roster and operate a staged swap process that avoids mass reingestion: active KV caches are drained and we prefer sticky routing so user-level sessions stay in-region where possible. We currently aim to provide 72 hours' notice for planned swappers and 24 hours for unplanned but non-emergency swaps. For emergency operator swaps (security or reliability incidents) we may act immediately and then notify — we will include an incident timeline and remediation report.

3) Telemetry & retention: We do not replicate request payloads outside the pinned region. Logs contain request IDs, timing, model variant, and non-identifying telemetry for debugging. Raw request payloads and embeddings are only stored in-region unless a customer explicitly enables cross-region analytics. Ephemeral traces used for debugging are purged within 7 days by default; we can negotiate shorter retention windows (e.g., 24–72 hours) in the DPA annex.

4) Attachments: attached is our public subprocessor_roster_v3.pdf and a proposed DPA annex template (dpa_annex_subprocessor_swap.docx). I've also attached a short KMS handling summary.

Next steps: I'll loop Marissa (Legal) and Jonas (Ops) to propose contract language and a short call to finalize the operational checklist. If you prefer 48 hours as a hard commitment, indicate that and we'll see what we can do commercially.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Product — Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v3.pdf, dpa_annex_subprocessor_swap.docx, kms-handling-summary.pdf
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency guarantees and operator/subprocessor swap policy — proposed contract language

Hi Lena —

Thanks Diego. Per MediCore's ask, we've drafted a short DPA annex snippet you can review; the attached Word contains the redline, but key points are below (proposed):

- Subprocessor Swap Notification: Redwood will provide a minimum of seventy-two (72) hours' advance written notice for planned subprocessor/operator changes that may result in cross-border processing. For customers requiring expedited notice, Redwood may agree to a forty-eight (48) hour notice by separate written amendment.

- Emergency Exceptions: In the event of a security incident or critical regional outage, Redwood may perform immediate operator swaps without prior notice to preserve availability. Redwood will provide an incident report within forty-eight (48) hours post-action and apply mitigations to avoid reprocessing of raw payloads across regions.

- KMS & Key Handling: Customer keys remain under the customer's KMS where requested; Redwood supports bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Private deployments. Temporary operator access to keys for incident recovery will be performed under strict, auditable controls and logged.

- Telemetry Retention: Any debugging traces containing customer payload identifiers will be purged within seventy-two (72) hours unless otherwise agreed. Aggregated telemetry for capacity/latency analysis is retained 90 days.

I've attached the redline: dpa_annex_subprocessor_swap.docx. Please review and send any markups. If MediCore wants 48h as a hard contractual SLA, we'll need to flag it as a commercial exception and capture it in the master services schedule.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-03T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency guarantees and operator/subprocessor swap policy — proposed contract language

Marissa —

Thanks for the redline. A few clarifications from our side:  

• 72h vs 48h: Our compliance team will push for 48h notice for planned swaps. We appreciate the exception path but would like to see pricing/crediting if Redwood cannot meet 48h for planned swaps. Can you outline what a commercial exception would look like?

• KMS: We run a hybrid KMS in our control plane for keys used to encrypt at-rest artifacts. We need confirmation that Redwood will not export key material or request plaintext keys during any recovery. The KMS summary was helpful, but could you confirm in writing that key material will never be escrowed by Redwood?

• Evidence: Please confirm you can produce the subprocessor roster export with effective dates and a change log for any swap events going back 12 months. That will satisfy our vendor evidence requirements.

We can do a 30-minute call next week to finalize. Samir and our Legal lead will join.

Best,
Lena
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Residency guarantees and operator/subprocessor swap policy — next steps

Lena —

Thanks — quick answers and next steps below:  

1) 48h commercial exception: We can offer a negotiated 48-hour planned-swap notice as a contract amendment for MediCore. The commercial exception will be captured in the Master Services Schedule (MSS) and is typically tied to a 12-month committed spend level; I'll have Sales & Finance draft the language. In cases where Redwood cannot meet the 48h notice due to emergent load or forced operator rotation, we propose a service credit equal to 5% of the monthly service fee for that month's impacted portion. We'll send a proposal via HubSpot to capture the variant (see link).

2) KMS/key material: Confirmed — Redwood does not escrow customer KMS key material nor will we request plaintext keys. For BYOK customers we support customer-managed keys in supported clouds (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). Any temporary operational decryption is performed by agents with ephemeral access, under HSM-enforced policies, and fully audited. See kms-handling-summary.pdf attached.

3) Subprocessor evidence: We will export the roster with effective dates and a change log for the prior 12 months. I attached subprocessor_roster_v3.pdf tonight; we'll also provide a CSV export for your Security team on request.

4) Call: I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment for Wednesday 2026-12-09 at 09:00 PT and send a calendar invite with the DPA redline and a short ops checklist. If that doesn't work for your Legal team, propose alternate times.

I'll also route the 48h commercial exception request through our Sales team and include proposed service credit language.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Diego
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
